input.content:
Let's be upfront about scope first

If you searched for "how to build a SaaS app with AI," you're probably picturing something that generates your entire product — frontend, backend, database, user accounts, billing, the works. Kodely doesn't do that today. It has no backend generation, no database, no auth, and no payments integration. What it does build, well, is a real Vite + React 19 + TypeScript + Tailwind CSS app from a plain-English description, with a live preview and a one-click public URL.

That's not a small thing. Before a single line of backend code matters, every SaaS needs a front door: a landing page that explains what the product does, why anyone should care, and where to sign up. This guide is about building that — a real, live, publishable SaaS landing page — with Kodely, today. If you're further along and need the actual application logic, you'll still be wiring that up with a developer or another tool; Kodely gets you the marketing layer fast so you're not blocked waiting on it.

Why the landing page comes first anyway

Most SaaS founders build the product before the landing page and then scramble to explain it. It usually works better in reverse:

  • A landing page forces you to state your value proposition in one sentence — before you've sunk weeks into features nobody asked for.
  • You can start collecting signups, running ads, or validating a waitlist while the product is still being built.
  • A live URL gives you something real to test messaging against, instead of guessing.

Kodely is built for exactly this kind of fast, iterative front-end work: describe the page, watch it compile in real time, publish it, and keep refining it in chat as your positioning changes.

What you're actually getting

To set expectations correctly, here's what a Kodely-built landing page is, concretely:

  • Real code, not a template. Every project starts from a genuine foundation with hand-built UI primitives (Button, Card, Section, Nav) and grows from there as you describe what you want.
  • A live preview that renders the actual compiled app as it's generated, so you see the real thing, not a mockup of it.
  • A free public URL at <yourname>.kodely.site the moment you hit Publish. No separate hosting step.
  • Checkpoints — every successful generation is a restore point, so you can experiment with a new hero section or pricing layout without fear of losing what worked.
  • A code view where you can read and copy the generated source. There's no zip export yet, so treat Kodely as where the page lives and runs, not a step before you download it elsewhere.

What it won't give you: a working signup flow that creates real accounts, a database storing your waitlist, or Stripe collecting real payments. The "Sign Up" and "Start Free Trial" buttons on your landing page will need to point somewhere — early on, that's often a waitlist form, an email link, or a Calendly booking, until your actual product (and its auth/billing) exists.

Building the page, step by step

1. Write one clear prompt describing the whole page

Kodely works best when you describe the sections you want and the tone, not just "build me a landing page." Be specific about your product name, who it's for, and what the core pitch is. The more concrete you are, the less back-and-forth you'll need afterward.

2. Let it generate, then read the live preview like a stranger would

Once Kodely compiles the app, look at it as a first-time visitor. Does the headline explain what the product does in five seconds? Is the call to action obvious? This is the fastest feedback loop you'll get before anyone real sees it.

3. Iterate in chat, section by section

Don't try to fix everything in one message. Ask for one change at a time — "make the hero headline shorter and lead with the outcome," "add a three-column feature grid under the hero," "add a pricing teaser section with three tiers." Kodely edits the real components each time, and every successful edit is a checkpoint you can roll back to for free if a change makes things worse.

4. Publish, then keep refining

Hit Publish and your page is live at <yourname>.kodely.site immediately. From there, treat it as a living page: as your positioning sharpens or you learn what messaging converts, go back into chat and describe the change. There's no rebuild-and-redeploy ritual — you describe it, it compiles, you publish again.

A prompt you can copy and adapt

Here's a real example for a fictional SaaS called Ledgerbird — an AI-powered invoicing and expense-tracking tool for freelancers. Swap in your own product details:

"Build a SaaS landing page for Ledgerbird, an AI tool that turns a freelancer's bank transactions into ready-to-send invoices and categorized expense reports. Audience is solo freelancers and independent contractors who hate bookkeeping. Include: a nav bar with the Ledgerbird name and a 'Get Started' button; a hero section with a bold headline about never manually invoicing again, a one-sentence subheadline, and a primary CTA button; a three-column feature section covering 'Auto-generated invoices,' 'Expense categorization,' and 'Tax-ready reports'; a simple three-tier pricing section (Starter, Pro, Business) with monthly prices and a short feature list per tier; a testimonial-style section with two short quotes from freelancers; and a footer CTA section repeating the sign-up button. Use a clean, modern style with a lot of white space and a single accent color."

From there, refine with follow-ups like "make the pricing section highlight the Pro tier as most popular" or "swap the accent color for a deep green." Each one is a small, specific edit — that's the pattern that works best.

Where the actual product fits in

Once your landing page is live and you're ready to build the real product — user accounts, a database, subscription billing — that's outside what Kodely does today. Plan on pairing your Kodely-built front door with a backend built separately (a developer, a backend-as-a-service platform, or your own stack). Kodely's job in that picture is to get your marketing site live fast and keep it easy to update as your product and pricing evolve, not to generate the backend itself.

Get started

Kodely gives new accounts 750 free credits with no card required, and a landing page like the one above typically costs somewhere in the range of a first small build — you'll see the exact credit cost before anything is charged, and a build that fails to compile is never billed. Head to /signup to start building, check /pricing if you want to see what credit top-ups cost once you outgrow the free tier, or browse /blog for more guides on what to build next.
